propositions: Parallel multi-session writes to the git-backed tickets store cause the compaction sweep to mutate the worktree (SNAPSHOT writes, *.retired renames, .archived deletions) before committing, with no rollback on worker death, leaving dirty trees that break git merge and strand local commits.

Compaction-time dirty trees make _union_merge's 'git merge origin/tickets' abort in two classes: (a) untracked files origin wants to create, and (b) tracked-file deletions/modifications; both variants strand local ticket commits and break plan-review/close attestation.
Runtime marker files (*/.archived, */.write.lock) are tracked in HEAD (committed before gitignore patterns existed) and never un-tracked, causing routine marker churn to show as tracked dirt forever.

Compaction must be crash-atomic: the fold commits as one unit with rollback on failure, an intent journal outside the worktree tracks fold state for crash recovery, and recovery reverts abandoned partial folds under the write lock before the dirty tree is produced.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must default to active tickets only and accept --include-archived to reach archived tickets, so scan cost tracks the active working set as the store grows.

fsck must detect dirty-tree and stale-lock classes (tracked deletions, untracked regenerable leftovers, orphaned locks), and doctor --repair must heal safe artifacts (restore, quarantine, reclaim) under the write lock.
